reason: I checked the verdict and could not break it. I-042 and I-128 stay closed, with no build and no probe. The recount of r7_miss710_out.json matches every number: 668 = 64 + 604 missing GT nodes; 1,211 FN edge-ends; 31 merges (30 yx, 1 z); 80 nodes pruned by the tail; 557 raw misses; 477 nodes at 7-10 um, of which 456 (96%) have an unclaimed nearest node; mean |dz| 4.74 um, |dyx| 5.65 um. The 7 um radius is the official max_distance (tools/official/src/tracking_cellmot/division_metrics.py:94). Rounding the coordinates copies the submission writer (CONTEXT l.812-813). The merge count covers every merge within 7 um. When a merged blob absorbs an unannotated neighbour, the Hungarian match still gives it to the lone GT node, so that case is never a miss. A z-split can reach at most the 1 z-dominant merge (2 FN edges). Even a yx-split would reach only 57 FN edges at 100% precision, and that is a different mechanism. Three parts of the recorded FACT are wrong or overstated, and they must be fixed before the curator stores it. (1) '96% claimed by no GT node' is only the annotation base rate: GT is ~1% annotated in 44b6 and ~9% in 6bba. I ran a control with the same 7 um Hungarian on exp60: for matched GT nodes whose nearest other final node lies at 7-10 um, that node is unclaimed 94.6% of the time in 44b6 and 97.6% in 6bba. The missing nodes give 92.7% and 95.9%, the same as the control, so this statistic says nothing about a 'localisation or identity class'. (2) The real signal is on the z axis. Among missing nodes at 7-10 um, the nearest final node is z-dominant in 41% of cases, against 25-28% in the control. That is an axial offset or elongation excess. The image evidence that this is not an under-segmentation is the v2 valley test on exp39, not the r7 script: only 4% of 326 misses at 7-10 um show an intensity valley, so the GT point and the peak sit on the same object (research/wf_ideas_v2/r1_hyp_detection.notes.md l.8). The r7 script cannot tell a neighbour-peak merge at 7-10 um from a displaced self-detection. (3) 6bba holds 436 of the 477 misses at 7-10 um (91%) and 604 of the 668 misses. The anatomy is therefore mostly one recording, and its private transfer is unknown. The claim that 'only retraining can reach it' is a judgement, not a measurement. It is still consistent with the closed training-free relocalisation lines (head-shift scale I-035, K2 lowrefine already in place, dogrescue refuted). Feasibility does not apply: nothing is built, and new mechanisms end at the R8 cutoff (27 Sep 12:00 UTC), in a class that went 0/5 on the LB.
fix: Record the FACT with this corrected wording: 'x138 (exp60, 56 clips, official 7 um match): 668 missing GT nodes / 1,211 FN edge-ends. Merges with an annotated neighbour 31 (4.6%; 30 yx, 1 z; complete for <= 7 um, because merges with an unannotated neighbour are not misses). Pruned by the tail 80 (12%). Absent upstream 557 (83%). Nearest final node at 7-10 um: 477 (71%; 6bba 436). Their nearest-node unclaimed rate equals the annotation base rate (control 94.6% / 97.6%), so it carries no information. They are z-dominant 41% vs 25-28% in the control, an axial offset excess. The v2 valley test (4% valley, exp39) says the GT point and the peak are on the same object.' Z-split / I-042 / I-128 stay closed (reachable: 1 z-merge, 2 FN edges). For the post-deadline lessons (R9), put 'axial localisation of z-elongated nuclei in 6bba' on the detector/head list, not 'identity class'. No build, no probe.
realistic_gain: 0 on public and private: the finding only records a fact, and the reachable z-merge ceiling is 1 node / 2 FN edges in 56 clips (<< +0.0001). The corrected wording helps only the post-deadline lessons: it points retraining at axial (z) localisation in 6bba-like embryos instead of an 'identity' class that the 96% statistic never supported.
